Privacy policy

rcclone · Effective October 13, 2026

This policy describes Eduardo Mena's personal Google OAuth application, rcclone, used with the open-source rclone tool to access his own Google Drive from his computer.

Google data accessed

With the account owner's authorization, rclone can access Google Drive file content and metadata, including names, folder structure, sizes, modification times, and storage usage. Its Drive permission supports listing, reading, downloading, creating, updating, and deleting files.

How the data is used

Google data is used to display and manage files in the mounted Drive folder and to carry out file operations requested by the account owner. The application does not sell Google user data, use it for advertising, or use it to train generalized artificial-intelligence or machine-learning models.

Storage and retention

Google Drive continues to store the cloud files. The installed rclone application stores its OAuth credentials on the account owner's computer and may keep downloaded files, cached file data, and diagnostic logs there. Local caches and logs may contain file names or other metadata.

Local data remains until removed by the configured cache policy or by the account owner. Files deliberately downloaded outside the cache remain until the account owner removes them. Revoking Google access does not automatically delete existing local copies.

Sharing and website hosting

The installed rclone application communicates with Google's services to perform the requested file operations. This informational website does not receive Google Drive content or OAuth credentials, and the personal application has no separate application server operated by Eduardo Mena.

These pages contain no analytics scripts, advertising, sign-in forms, or data-submission forms. GitHub Pages hosts them and may process technical request information, such as IP addresses, to provide and secure its service. See the GitHub Privacy Statement and Google Privacy Policy for those providers' practices.

Revoking access and deleting local data

The account owner can revoke rcclone's access in Google Account connections. After any pending uploads finish and the mount is stopped, the account owner can remove rclone's saved remote configuration, caches, logs, and downloaded copies from the computer. Deleting files through an active Drive mount can also delete those files from Google Drive.

Contact and updates

Questions about this personal application or its handling of data can be sent to Eduardo Mena at edujxa@gmail.com. Updates to this policy will be posted on this page with a revised effective date.
